messages.subject: Nestedness in measurement invariance
parts:
Hi all, 

I did a measurement invariance for a perception of child to their father's child rearing and to their mother's child rearing. More specifically, I assessed whether one child interpret his/her father's child rearing similarly to his/her mother's child rearing. After establishing the invariance I compared latent mean different across two type of child rearing with a child.
To do so, I put the report of perception of the child rearing in two groups. Technically, I can put the two groups in the an argument in the cfa() of the lavaan, for example , group = "perception_group". However, I am wondering whether lavaan can still assign each pair of perception in its corresponding ID (case). That is the comparison should be in conducted within the same ID. Maybe there will be a situation that a perception of father's child rearing of a child will be compared to mother's child rearing of another child.  Can anyone tell me whether the mismatch can happen and if so how I can control this? Maybe I need to put an option of clustering to control this? But I have no experience on it.

Can anyone help me out with this please?

Thank you so much in advance for your time, 

Best regards, 

Torres

messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: Re: Nestedness in measurement invariance
parts:
Hi all, 

I think I had an answer for that after reading some papers of Jak, Jorgensen and Rosseel. The data children's perception of parent's child rearing can be nested within a cluster of family's data (fathers and mothers). The model for the test is the two-level model, which is used to examine measurement invariance across levels. 

You can have a look at the papers I already read above

Jak, S., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2017). Relating measurement invariance, cross-level invariance, and multilevel reliability. Frontiers in psychology, 8, 1640.

Jak, S., Jorgensen, T. D., & Rosseel, Y. (2021). Evaluating Cluster-Level Factor Models with lavaan and Mplus. Psych, 3(2), 134-152.

Best, 
Torres

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Nestedness in measurement invariance
parts:
Glad you found our multilevel invariance paper, but I would not recommend multilevel SEM for this case.  You specifically want to compare the children's perceptions of their mothers to their perceptions of their fathers.  These are not multiple independent groups.  They are repeated measures of the same child.  So you need to evaluate what is typically called a "longitudinal" measurement invariance, even though it is really just invariance for any kind of dependent "groups" or repeated measures.  Store the data in wide format, with mother variables in different columns than father variables, so there is one row per child.  Then you fit a CFA with separate factors for mothers and fathers, and test whether their measurement parameters are equivalent, similar to the procedure used for testing invariance across groups.  But you have to explicitly use labels to make equality constraints.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
